title: Per-token timing probes and multi-region failover telemetry + runbook
creator: Avery Collins
summary: Add fine-grained per-token timing probes across request paths, expose multi-region failover signals, and deliver a runbook + Grafana dashboards to diagnose SLO degradation quickly.
description: Problem: We currently lack consistent, low-noise instrumentation that ties per-token latency patterns to multi-region failover events and circuit breaker activations. When SLO alerts fire we spend significant time reconstructing tokenization characteristics, admission decisions, and cross-region fallbacks. Goal: (1) instrument per-token timing probes across key decode/encode stages with sampling controls and low overhead; (2) surface synthesized multi-region failover metrics (region-switch count, last-fallback-reason) and circuit state transitions to the same dashboards; (3) ship a concise runbook that guides on- call diagnosis and automated mitigation (e.g., progressive load-shedding, model variant fallback). This ticket covers the instrumentation schema, pipeline changes, dashboard panels, and the initial runbook draft.
acceptance_criteria: Per-token timing probes implemented for request lifecycle stages: tokenizer, model-forward, kv-lookup, decode-step, and response-serialize (sampling rate configurable to 0.1%..100%)
New telemetry fields added to traces/metrics: token_position, token_type (wordpiece|bpe), kv_hit, region_origin, region_target, circuit_state (OPEN|CLOSED|HALF_OPEN), failover_reason

Grafana dashboard with at least 6 panels: per-token p50/p95/p99 heatmap, avg model-forward by token position, kv-hit correlation with latency, per-region fallback rates, circuit-state timeline, synthetic-route p95 overlay
Alerting rules updated to incorporate token-level regressions (detect p95 token-position shift > 30% over 5m) and multi-region spike correlation
Runbook published in Confluence with triage steps, mitigation playbook and links to dashboards and PRs
CPU/GPU overhead of added probes < 3% at 1% sampling in production canary
Telemetry fields documented in our observability schema and backwards-compatible with existing ingestion pipelines
plan: Design: finalize schema for per-token probes and failover signals (observability@ meeting 2026-02-24)
Proto: implement lightweight probes behind a feature flag; sample 1% traffic; emit metrics to prometheus histograms and traces to jaeger
Pipeline: add enrichment step to tag region_target and failover_reason in the aggregator service
Dashboards: build Grafana panels and a lightweight single-page incident view for on-call
Runbook: draft Confluence page with reproducible playbook and example mitigations
Rollout: canary (10%) -> regional ramp -> global enable with monitoring for overhead and false positives
updates: 2026-02-22: Design reviewed with SRE and runtime teams. Decision: use histogram+trace dual approach to balance overhead and fidelity. Agreed sampling tiers: 0.1%, 1%, 5%.
2026-03-01: Prototype pushed behind flag in inference-proxy (PR: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/1426). Initial microbench shows ~1.8% CPU at 1% sample on x86 serving nodes.

2026-03-04: Telemetry schema proposal posted to #observability for review (doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Per-Token+Probe+Schema). Feedback: rename 'decode-step' to 'token_decode' for clarity and add 'kv_latency_ms' field.
2026-03-08: Aggregator enrichment implemented (PR: github.com/redwood/telemetry/pull/389). It tags traces with region_target and failover_reason when a fallback occurs. Integration tests added.
2026-03-10: First Grafana draft deployed to staging dashboards (panel ids: 8221, 8222, 8223). SRE asks for a combined heatmap that overlays p95 with kv_hit rate — added to next iteration.

2026-03-12: Canary rollout to 5% production traffic enabled. Monitoring for overhead and alert noise initiated. Observed a noisy spike in token-position p95 for a single customer due to long-context workload; created follow-up ENG-572015 to add customer-tagged rollouts.
comments: Avery Collins (2026-02-25): Note from design review — prefer histogram buckets aligned with model sequence lengths (8, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512) to simplify aggregation.

Rajat Mehra (2026-03-02): Prototype PR shows decode-step timers are hot; we should coalesce small timers to reduce cardinality. Proposal: only emit per-token timers for positions 0..64 and aggregate 'tail' positions as a group.
Maya Lopez (SRE, 2026-03-05): Add an automated synthetic query that exercises failover routing to produce deterministic event for dashboard smoke tests.
Product (2026-03-07): We need the runbook to include customer-visible status wording for incidents that trigger cross-region failover — include suggested messaging templates.

Security (2026-03-09): Confirm that token content is never logged. Observability fields must use token_position and token_type only; token text must be redacted. We'll sign off once the aggregator enforces redaction.
